3.1a — The Turret: Distance & the Detection Radius

The turret is your first adversary that decides. Its whole brain, today, is one number: how far away are you? One if-statement separates "asleep" from "shooting." Every boss you build later starts from this exact idea.

Predict First ~10 min

Read TurretController.cs — the turret's awareness, in full:

[SerializeField] private float maxAttackRange = 7f;
...
private void Update()
{
    float distanceToPlayer = Vector3.Distance(transform.position, playerController.transform.position);

    if (distanceToPlayer <= maxAttackRange)
    {
        // (today: just watch the boundary; the shooting comes in 3.2a)
    }
}

Predict before running: you creep toward the turret. At what distance does it "see" you — exactly 7, or 6.99, or 7.01? What happens when you stand exactly on the boundary and jitter one pixel in and out? Write your prediction; the Debug.Log in the lab will settle it.

Socratic

Vector3.Distance is a function someone else wrote — square roots inside, probably. You call it without ever seeing the math. What is that hiding called on the AP exam, and what would your movement code from 1.4a look like if you had to write Translate from raw matrix math every time?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — place a turret and read its knob. Drag the Turret prefab into the Overworld, select it, and find Max Attack Range in the Inspector: 7. The turret's brain is a serialized float, exactly like your xSpeed. Everything about its difficulty lives in tunable numbers.

Step 2 — see the number live. Add this to the turret's Update for today (delete it after — it is a measurement, not a feature):

Debug.Log(distanceToPlayer);

Walk toward the turret and watch the Console. Stop at the moment the number crosses 7.0 — did anything visible change? (Not yet: the shooting fires nothing today. You are watching the condition, in the raw.)

Step 3 — the boundary experiment. Stand at the edge: the condition is <=, so 7.0 counts. Now change it to < and stand exactly at 7.0 (use the Inspector readout of the player's transform to get surgical). What does <= vs < change about the game? One pixel of fairness — the same trap the AP exam tests with list indexes.

Bug Hunt: The blind turret

  1. Set maxAttackRange to 0.5 and stand away. Why does "shrinking the radius" produce the same behavior as deleting the turret — and what is the design lesson?
  2. Move the player out of the scene (delete the Player GameObject from the Hierarchy) and press Play. What does the Console say, and which line of Start() wrote that message?
  3. Comment out the Distance call and hardcode float distanceToPlayer = 3f;. What did you just build — a turret that always shoots, or one that never does?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Design the aggro

  1. Tune maxAttackRange by playtesting: what feels right — 5? 9? 12? Where does "scary" become "unfair"? Write your winner and one sentence why.
  2. Design: should the turret keep its detection radius a secret from the player, or telegraph it? How would a designer SHOW a 7-unit radius without printing numbers?
  3. Hard: could you build a turret that only sees you in one direction (a cone)? What other function would you need besides distance? Sketch the idea; you will actually build it in the boss unit.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain what Vector3.Distance returns and use it in a condition
  • Predict the <= boundary case and verify it live
  • Explain why the turret finds the player by tag in Start, not Update
  • Tune maxAttackRange like a designer, with evidence
